articles.title: Slotkin lawyer warns Blanche not to obey Trump’s ‘frivolous’ demand to investigate her
articles.summary: The Michigan senator’s speech seeking to deter young people from joining the administration was “entirely lawful,” her lawyer wrote in a letter.
articles.body:
WASHINGTON — An attorney for Democratic Sen. Elissa Slotkin of Michigan warned Attorney General Todd Blanche not to bow to President Donald Trump's demand for a criminal investigation into her political speech.

Over the weekend, Trump said on Truth Social that he was demanding the Justice Department look into Slotkin's recent comments about how Democratic investigations into the Trump administration could send a "deterrence message" to young people thinking about joining the administration in its final two years.

"By copy of this statement, I am ordering the Department of Justice to look into this criminal act, immediately!" Trump wrote.

In a letter to Blanche made public Monday, Preet Bharara, the former U.S. attorney in the Southern District of New York, wrote that it "should not be hard to make clear that we do not live in an authoritarian regime where mere criticism of the powerful can land anyone in legal peril and possibly prison."

"That requires a clear and public statement confirming that the Department will not pursue this investigation against Senator Slotkin," he wrote.

The Justice Department didn't comment on Trump's post. In a statement Monday, a Justice Department spokesperson declined to rule out an investigation.

"Sen. Slotkin said publicly that the prospect of future investigations should deter young people from joining this administration," the spokesperson said. "The Department believes public service should not be met with threats of retribution, and this Department is committed to ending the weaponization of government. We follow the facts and the law."

The attorney general is appointed by the president and is a member of his Cabinet, but it's still highly unusual for the White House to publicly demand an investigation. The Justice Department has long sought to separate politics from the law. But under Blanche , Trump's former personal attorney, the department has investigated many of the president's perceived political enemies .

Slotkin, a former CIA and Defense Department official, was also one of a group of lawmakers the Trump administration tried and failed to indict earlier this year over a social media video .

A few weeks before the midterm elections, where the GOP saw massive losses, she spoke at the University of Chicago , arguing that Democrats should focus investigative efforts on those who enable Trump. She said she hoped to deter young people coming out of school from joining the administration.

"I want them to be like, 'Lord, that might be buying myself a ton of problems that I don't want, and so let me avoid participating in that,'" Slotkin said. "I want that deterrence message sent."

In his post on Truth Social over the weekend, Trump accused Slotkin of "going to go after all young people that believe in Republican Values, and that give even the slightest inclination to be a Republican."

Trump's demand came weeks after Trump ally Mike Davis asked that Harmeet Dhillon — who has since resigned as head of the Civil Rights Division — launch an investigation of Slotkin.

Bharara wrote that Slotkin's comments were "entirely lawful" and protected by the First Amendment as well as the "speech and debate" clause of the Constitution, which protects members of Congress.

"There is no conceivable basis to investigate the Senator for reminding members of the executive branch who aid the President's law breaking that there will be accountability for their actions, or expressing the hope that Americans decline to serve in an administration where leaders may ask them to violate the law or misuse taxpayer dollars," Bharara wrote. "Indeed, the Senator's statement reinforces the rule of law."

Bharara asked Blanche to publicly decline to follow Trump's command.

"The Department should stop threatening our constitutional freedoms and make clear that you will not again launch another frivolous investigation at the taxpayers' expense," he wrote.

Bharara's letter noted that it had been less than a year since the administration failed to indict Slotkin and five other members of Congress over a social media video that reminded members of the military and intelligence communities of their duties not to follow unlawful orders.

"Thankfully, the anonymous citizens of a Washington D.C. grand jury unanimously rejected the Department's attempt to punish a perceived political adversary for her lawful — indeed, constitutionally privileged — speech," Bharara wrote.

images.caption: President Donald Trump over the weekend demanded that Attorney General Todd Blanche and the Justice Department investigate Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich. (Getty )

articles.title: John Fetterman to be challenged for Senate seat by democratic socialist born in Gaza
articles.summary: Ahmed Moor, a Palestinian American, said he would run in a primary to be the Democratic nominee in 2028
articles.body:
John Fetterman, the maverick Democratic senator who has provoked widespread anger by increasingly siding with Republicans, is to be challenged for his Pennsylvania seat by a democratic socialist candidate who is originally from Gaza.

Ahmed Moor, a Palestinian American, said he would run in a primary to be the Democratic nominee in 2028, when Fetterman's seat is up for re-election.

The move is the first sign of Fetterman's weakened position in the party since the Democrats won back control of the Senate in last week's US midterm elections, when the party won at least 54 of the upper chamber's 100 seats.

The prospect of a comfortable Senate majority in effect eliminates the possibility of Fetterman's vote being decisive, a relief to Democratic strategists who feared he could no longer be relied on for support on contentious issues.

Fetterman had already caused widespread disillusionment among many Pennsylvania Democrats, who campaigned for him in the 2022 midterms when he ran as a progressive outsider.

But he has sparked anger by, on occasion, speaking out in support of Donald Trump, who in turn has praised Fetterman as "a great guy" and said he would "love" him to become a Republican.

Moor, 42, a writer and journalist who was born in the southern Gaza city of Rafah and has previously written for the Guardian, told the Philadelphia Inquirer that he was "not really running against Fetterman".

"I'm running for good government. I'm running for the rule of law. I'm running because I believe in America," he said.

But his Palestinian background throws down the gauntlet to Fetterman's vocally pro-Israel stance, which has become increasingly strident since the 7 October 2023 attack by Hamas that left about 1,200 people on the Israeli side dead. More than 74,000 Palestinians in Gaza – most women and children – have been killed in Israel's retaliatory military response.

Fetterman has said he has no intention of leaving the Democrats but strongly suggested would change his mind if the party became "anti-Israel".

"That's my red line," Fetterman said last July. "If the Democratic party becomes official anti-Israel, then that's when I would force me out. If they make it the official platform of the party, then that's a much different situation."

Fetterman has met more often with Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's prime minister, than with Philadelphia's mayor, Cherelle Parker, according to the Philadelphia Inquirer.

Moor, by contrast, said he supports withdrawing US aid from Israel and imposing sanctions aimed at securing equal rights for Palestinians.

Democrats say Moor is unlikely to be the only challenger to Fetterman, who provoked outrage in his own party in September by sending a video message to the Republicans' midterm convention in Texas in which he praised Pennsylvania's Republican senator, Dave McCormick.

"I'm pretty confident that you'll see some bigger, mainstream kind of names, involved," said Mike Weidinger, a veteran Lancaster county Democrat with state-wide connections, who cited Chris Deluzio, a representative from the Pittsburgh area, and Malcolm Kenyatta, a Pennsylvania state legislator, as likely challengers.

"Generally, people think [Fetterman] either misrepresented himself when he ran the first time, or he changed completely from what he said he was," said Weidinger.

"We just had an election here in Pennsylvania where a lot of us busted our ass for [Pennsylvania governor Josh] Shapiro and a lot of other people, and he didn't spend one penny or do one thing for a single Democrat candidate here last week."

On the possibility of Fetterman joining the Republicans, he added: "If he wants to switch, he can switch. If it would have been 51 to 49, it would have mattered. But it doesn't matter now."

articles.title: PF vai refazer relatórios sobre ministros do STF citados no caso Master | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo interlocutores da corporação, documentos anteriores não seguiram critérios definidos por Fachin. Novos textos serão individualizados, trarão contexto das citações e não farão análises.
articles.summary: Segundo interlocutores da corporação, documentos anteriores não seguiram critérios definidos por Fachin. Novos textos serão individualizados, trarão contexto das citações e não farão análises.
articles.body:
A Polícia Federal (PF) vai refazer os relatórios sobre as menções a ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) encontradas nas investigações do caso Master, segundo interlocutores da corporação.

Essas mesmas fontes afirmam que, na avaliação da corporação, os documentos anteriores, produzidos por dois delegados afastados de funções de chefia na semana passada, não seguiram os critérios determinados pelo presidente do STF, ministro Edson Fachin .

Os relatórios serão individualizados sobre todos os ministros do STF que tenham sido citados, e não apenas Alexandre de Moraes, Kassio Nunes Marques e Dias Toffoli. O blog do Valdo Cruz mostrou que também há menções aos ministros André Mendonça, Luiz Fux e Gilmar Mendes .

Os novos relatórios vão apresentar as referências aos ministros em trocas de mensagens com o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro e os contextos em que elas aparecem , com informações como a identidade do interlocutor, a data e o horário da conversa.

➡️ Para respeitar os critérios definidos por Fachin, os relatórios não vão trazer nenhum tipo de análise sobre o conteúdo dessas mensagens.

A orientação para que as informações fossem apresentadas de forma descritiva foi dada por Edson Fachin em 13 de outubro, após uma reunião com Andrei Rodrigues, diretor-geral da PF.

Na ocasião, o presidente do STF afirmou que “todas as menções encontradas sem exceção” a ministros da Corte no caso Master deveriam ser encaminhadas ao Supremo , acompanhadas de seu contexto e em “caráter estritamente descritivo”.

Edson Fachin também afirmou que uma eventual investigação contra um ministro depende de autorização do plenário do STF.

Na segunda-feira (9), investigadores da PF concluíram três relatórios com menções aos ministros Dias Toffoli, Alexandre de Moraes e Kassio Nunes Marques.

Os documentos foram elaborados pelos delegados Daniel Cola e Wedson Cajé, responsáveis pelo caso Master, que foram afastados de suas funções na Coordenadoria-Geral de Repressão à Corrupção, Crimes Financeiros e Lavagem de Dinheiro no dia seguinte à conclusão dos relatórios.

➡️ A Polícia Federal não informou o motivo para o afastamento dos dois.

Na ocasião, a direção-geral da PF afirmou que os relatórios ainda estavam sendo elaborados e que seriam entregues ao Supremo até o fim de novembro.

Fachin determinou que a PF encaminhe todas as menções a ministros encontradas nas investigações, sem exceção, com o contexto em que aparecem e sem avançar sobre uma eventual investigação das autoridades.

Caberá ao Supremo decidir se há elementos para autorizar o aprofundamento das investigações sobre algum ministro.

Veja as citações aos ministros do STF já reveladas:

Toffoli integra o quadro de sócios da Maridt Participações, empresa familiar dirigida pelos irmãos do magistrado e que fez negócios com um fundo gerido pela empresa Reag, ligada ao Banco Master .

O plenário do STF chegou a se reunir em 15 de outubro, em sessão extraordinária, para julgar o relatório que apontou vínculo entre Moraes e Vorcaro.

O julgamento, no entanto, foi suspenso após apresentação de questão de ordem pelos ministros GIlmar e Dino , sem que o mérito do caso, ou seja, a abertura ou não de investigação sobre Moraes fosse analisado.

Em relação a Kassio Nunes Marques, a PF encontrou no celular de Vorcaro um contrato de prestação de serviços entre o Banco Master e um escritório de advocacia.

Mensagens trocadas por Vorcaro com Luiz Rennó, ex-diretor jurídico do Master, mencionam ainda supostos pagamentos de R$ 500 mil por mês ao advogado Kevin Marques, filho do ministro Nunes Marques .

O nome do ministro também surgiu em troca de mensagens sobre a organização de uma festa por Vorcaro para Nunes Marques com garotas de programa .

O advogado Ciro Rocha Soares, próximo de Vorcaro, chegou a enviar uma mensagem ao ex-banqueiro discutindo um suposto encontro com Mendonça.

Segundo nota divulgada pelo gabinete do ministro à época em que o caso foi revelado, o assunto no encontro tratado foi a Suspensão de Tutela Provisória (STP) 976, que estava sob julgamento do STF.

O caso discutia créditos de precatórios de interesse do Master, mas se encontrava, na data da reunião, sob pedido de vista.

O Banco Master comprou fatias milionárias de precatórios que estão na mira da PF devido a suspeitas de que foram expedidos pela Justiça antes do fim dos processos. A prática seria irregular, porque a União ainda podia recorrer e contestar o valor das dívidas.

articles.title: Prêmio Paulo Gustavo: Câmara homenageia destaques do humor em 2026 | G1
articles.standfirst: Prêmio leva o nome do ator e humorista que morreu de Covid-19. Em 2026, foram homenageados Carol Delgado, Clarice Falcão, Fábio Porchat, Marcus Majella e o Clube Dazminina.
articles.summary: O Prêmio Paulo Gustavo reconheceu o talento de Fábio Porchat, Clarice Falcão e outros humoristas na Câmara em cerimônia que celebrou o riso como ato de resistência.
articles.body:
Humoristas recebem prêmio Paulo Gustavo em cerimônia na Câmara dos Deputados — Foto: Júlia Christine/g1

A Comissão de Cultura da Câmara dos Deputados homenageou nesta terça-feira (10) nomes brasileiros que se destacaram por suas contribuições à cultura por meio do humor e da comédia.

O reconhecimento faz parte do Prêmio Paulo Gustavo, criado em homenagem ao ator e humorista que morreu de Covid-19, em maio de 2021.

A cerimônia foi realizada no Salão Nobre da Câmara dos Deputados, em Brasília, e contou com a participação da ministra da Cultura, Margareth Menezes.

Neste ano, foram homenageados Carol Delgado, Clarice Falcão , Fábio Porchat, Marcus Majella e o grupo Clube Dazminina. Os artistas receberam um diploma de menção honrosa.

A indicação de artistas, personalidades, grupos ou organizações é feita por parlamentares. A escolha dos homenageados fica a cargo de um conselho deliberativo, composto pelo segundo-secretário da Câmara e por integrantes da Comissão de Cultura.

Criada por uma resolução da Câmara de 2021, a premiação é realizada anualmente desde 2023.

Fábio Porchat foi um dos humoristas homenageados pela Câmara dos Deputados nesta terça-feira — Foto: Júlia Christine/g1

Um dos premiados nesta terça-feira, o ator Fábio Porchat relembrou a amizade com Paulo Gustavo e afirmou que rir também é um ato de "resistência".

"A verdade é que rir é resistência, porque é isso que nos faz vencer esses poderosos que estão o tempo inteiro apontando o dedo e dizendo que a gente não merece ser feliz, não merece rir, não merece ser quem a gente é. E é rindo que a gente fala não: 'Ninguém vai decidir quando eu vou dar risada'", afirmou Porchat.

Ministra da Cultura, Margareth Menezes destacou que Paulo Gustavo dá nome a uma lei de socorro ao setor cultural aprovada pelo Congresso durante a pandemia e que, atualmente, viabiliza investimentos diretos na área.

"Uma boa piada nos faz pensar sobre o racismo, o machismo, a desigualdade, a homofobia e tantos preconceitos que ainda precisamos enfrentar. Paulo Gustavo é a prova de que a arte pode transformar o destino, um menino de Niterói (RJ) que transformou as histórias da sua própria casa e das suas obras", disse a ministra.

A deputada Carol Dartora ( PT -PR), presidente da Comissão de Cultura da Câmara, classificou o humor como uma "expressão potente da cultura nacional".

"Fazer rir exige muita inteligência, muita capacidade, muita empatia, então o humor é de fato um dos nossos instrumentos que mais nos humaniza", declarou a petista.

Cerimônia de entrega do Prêmio Paulo Gustavo contou com a participação da ministra da Cultura, Margareth Menezes — Foto: Júlia Christine/g1

O ator, humorista e roteirista Paulo Gustavo morreu em decorrência da Covid-19, em maio de 2021, aos 42 anos. Ele construiu uma carreira de sucesso no teatro, na televisão e no cinema, principalmente com a franquia “Minha Mãe é uma Peça”.

Seu estilo de humor era marcado por situações familiares e cotidianas. Juntos, os três filmes da franquia venderam mais de 26 milhões de ingressos entre 2013 e 2020.

O terceiro longa alcançou a maior bilheteria da história do cinema brasileiro, com R$ 182 milhões em arrecadação.

Paulo Gustavo Amaral Monteiro de Barros nasceu em Niterói, no Rio de Janeiro, em 30 de outubro de 1978. Ele estudou teatro na Casa das Artes de Laranjeiras, no Rio, na mesma turma de Fábio Porchat, um dos homenageados pelo prêmio em 2026.

Paulo Gustavo, em foto de novembro de 2016 — Foto: Daniela Ramiro/Estadão Conteúdo/Arquivo

articles.title: Diretor da PF deixa associação dos delegados após 24 anos | G1
articles.summary: Andrei Rodrigues deixou a ADPF alegando divergências ideológicas e falta de apoio institucional após ser alvo de decisões judiciais do Supremo Tribunal Federal.
articles.body:
O diretor-geral da Polícia Federal , Andrei Rodrigues, desligou-se da Associação Nacional dos Delegados da PF (ADPF) após 24 anos filiado à entidade.

🔎A ADPF é uma associação criada para representar e defender as prerrogativas, a autonomia e os interesses dos delegados da PF. A associação também atua no debate sobre projetos de lei e em causas na Justiça ligadas à categoria.

Andrei formalizou sua saída da ADPF na última sexta-feira (6). A interlocutores, o diretor-geral da Polícia Federal disse que tomou a decisão por divergências político-ideológicas com a cúpula da entidade.

A pessoas próximas, Andrei também fez críticas à diretoria da ADPF, que, na avaliação do diretor, não se manifestou em defesa da PF quando a instituição foi alvo de críticas de parlamentares.

Segundo aliados, o diretor da PF também ficou incomodado com o que chamou de falta de apoio da ADPF quando Andrei foi afastado do cargo por decisão do ministro André Mendonça , do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ).

🔎Em setembro de 2026, Mendonça determinou o afastamento preventivo de Andrei e do diretor de inteligência da corporação , Leandro Almada, sob a acusação de monitoramento ilegal e "arapongagem institucional" contra o próprio magistrado e contra o advogado-geral da União, Jorge Messias .

A interlocutores, Andrei também declarou considerar que a ADPF não tem atuado em favor de reivindicações remuneratórias de superintendentes e diretores da PF e que a entidade tem agido contra o comando da Academia Nacional de Polícia.

A desfiliação de Andrei da ADPF é mais um elemento na divisão interna da Polícia Federal nos últimos meses.

Nesta terça-feira (10), veio a público a informação de que delegados da PF terão de refazer relatórios sobre as menções a ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) encontradas nas investigações do caso Master.

Interlocutores da corporação afirmam que os documentos anteriores, produzidos por dois delegados afastados de funções de chefia na semana passada, não seguiram os critérios determinados pelo presidente do STF, ministro Edson Fachin.

Os novos relatórios vão apresentar as menções aos ministros em trocas de mensagens com o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro e os contextos em que elas aparecem, com informações como a identidade do interlocutor, a data e o horário da conversa.

➡️ Para respeitar os critérios definidos por Fachin, os relatórios não vão trazer nenhum tipo de análise sobre o conteúdo dessas mensagens.

Cúpula da ADPF reage à desfiliação de Andrei

Integrantes da cúpula da ADPF afirmam considerar "anômalo" que o diretor-geral determine que um relatório de apuração seja refeito.

Eles também divergem de declarações sobre suposta atuação político-ideológica da entidade. E afirmam que a entidade defende princípios e apoiou policiais que foram alvos de ataques.

Para integrantes da ADPF, a atual direção da PF é que tem atuado politicamente . Membros da ADPF afirmam ser contrários a essa postura.

articles.title: CNJ aprova novas regras para venda de precatórios e cria central nacional para tentar rastrear operações | G1
articles.standfirst: Texto pretende criar cadeia de rastreamento por meio de exigências para cessão de crédito. Compra e venda de precatórios é um dos principais pontos da investigação que mira fraudes do Banco Master.
articles.summary: Texto pretende criar cadeia de rastreamento por meio de exigências para cessão de crédito. Compra e venda de precatórios é um dos principais pontos da investigação que mira fraudes do Banco Master.
articles.body:
O Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ) aprovou nesta terça-feira (10), por unanimidade, uma resolução com regras para a venda de precatórios, que prevê a criação de uma central nacional para rastrear as operações.

A relatora, Andréa Cunha Esmeraldo, afirmou que a matéria amplia a transparência e fortalece a governança da política judiciário de precatórios.

A compra e venda de precatórios é um dos principais pontos da investigação que mira fraudes do Banco Master ( leia mais abaixo ).

“Em última análise, busca ampliar a transparência e conferir maior segurança jurídica, exceções de créditos aos atos de pagamento e as respectivas de base baixos em benefício da eficiência administrativa e da adequação da adequada gestão dessas operações no âmbito do Poder Judiciário”, afirmou.

Entre outros pontos, a resolução aprovada estabelece que a transferência de um precatório para produzir efeitos dependerá do cumprimento conjunto de uma série de requisitos, como:

exige escritura pública de cessão do crédito;

registro eletrônico em entidade registradora;

comunicação à Central Nacional de Cessões de Créditos de Precatórios, criada pelo texto;

Na prática, as exigências pretendem criar uma cadeia de rastreamento do precatório. Sem o cumprimento das exigências, não será possível alterar a titularidade do precatório, habilitar o comprador para receber os recursos, emitir certidão do valor líquido em seu nome nem realizar o pagamento.

“Não tenho dúvida alguma da importância da disciplina da cessão de créditos de precatórios, dos ônus e garantias da incidência desses créditos e da Central Nacional da Cessão de Créditos de Precatórios. Estamos atendendo com isso segurança jurídica, rastreabilidade e transparência”, afirmou o presidente do CNJ e do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), Edson Fachin .

Conforme o texto, a Central Nacional de Cessões de Créditos de Precatórios será responsável por consolidar os atos referentes à venda de precatórios, como negociação, escritura, homologação, garantias, pagamento e outras movimentações envolvendo o crédito.

A resolução entra em vigor 30 dias após a data de sua publicação.

Peças de luxo do Banco Master vão a leilão para pagar credores — Foto: Jornal Nacional

O banco adquiria créditos de precatórios de empresas – principalmente, do setor sucroalcooleiro – com deságio, ou seja, por um valor mais baixo do que os títulos poderiam vir a valer após o fim de um processo judicial.

Posteriormente, após fraudes financeiras ou mera declaração irreal de valores, o banco registrava esses "precatórios a receber" como parte de seu patrimônio. Na prática, os papéis valeriam menos do que o registrado na contabilidade.

Ao registrar precatórios e créditos duvidosos por valores superiores aos reais, o Banco Master forjava uma aparência de riqueza, parecendo muito mais sólido do que a realidade.

Isso era utilizado para justificar aportes de capital e atender a exigências formais de saúde financeira impostas pelos órgãos fiscalizadores, em especial pelo Banco Central.

Com a suposta solidez atestada por esses ativos, a instituição conseguiu atrair investidores, movimentar bilhões em fundos e negociar operações de grande porte, acumulando um passivo bilionário ocultado por garantias de baixa qualidade.

“A proposta apresentada representa significativo avanço na disciplina da matéria. É um marco importante para a sociedade brasileira. Se mostra oportuna e institucionalmente relevante ao estabelecer nacional diretrizes para a concessão de crédito precatório, bem como para ônus e garantias, mecanismos de controle correlatos, inclusive mediante a instituição da Central Nacional de Cessão de Créditos e Precatórios”, destacou a relatora.

Para receber o precatório antes, credores acabam vendendo o direito de receber por um valor menor a instituições.

Conforme o texto, deverá constar na escritura, um dos pré-requisitos para a transferência do precatório, o deságio, em valor absoluto e em percentual.

Segundo o texto, a escritura deverá informar o valor atualizado do crédito, o valor líquido disponível, a parcela negociada e o preço pago.

Também deverão constar os custos notariais e de registro, a remuneração do intermediário e o valor líquido que ficará com o vendedor.​ ​

A proposta aprovada estabelece ainda que pessoas físicas que não atuem no mercado de precatórios, quando forem vender os créditos, deverão comparecer pessoalmente ao cartório.

O texto aprovado é fruto de uma nota técnica assinada por Fachin e o presidente do Banco Central, Gabriel Galípolo.

“Também aqui merece reconhecimento da articulação institucional entre esse conselho e o Banco Central nesta matéria. Os estudos técnicos do Banco Central contribuíram para o desenvolvimento dos trabalhos e permitiram também avançar nesse conciliado controle administrativo judicial das cessões com a infraestrutura registral necessária para a segurança dessas operações”, afirmou o presidente do CNJ.

articles.title: Senado prevê gasto de R$ 6 milhões com iPhones e outros celulares | G1
articles.standfirst: Edital prevê 425 celulares em comodato por quatro anos e determina a substituição dos aparelhos após dois anos.
articles.summary: Edital prevê 425 celulares em comodato por quatro anos e determina a substituição dos aparelhos após dois anos.
articles.body:
Plenário do Senado Federal — Foto: Jonas Pereira/Agência Senado

O Senado prevê gastar pouco mais de R$ 6 milhões em um contrato de serviços de telefonia que inclui o fornecimento de 95 iPhones 18 Pro, o mais recente da Apple, e 330 smartphones de outros modelos. A contratação prevê também chips de dados, modems e serviços como ligações e roaming internacional.

Os aparelhos serão fornecidos em regime de comodato — uma espécie de empréstimo — e deverão ser substituídos após dois anos de uso. A regra vale para os celulares dos dois tipos previstos no edital: os iPhones e os modelos intermediários.

A substituição após dois anos, segundo o documento, será feita por causa da “evolução tecnológica”. No caso dos iPhones, o edital determina que o novo aparelho seja “o melhor aparelho da categoria 'high end' disponível para o mercado corporativo e que atenda aos requisitos técnicos estabelecidos".

O Senado diz que a contratação dos serviços "é indispensável para garantir o adequado desempenho das atividades institucionais, assegurando conectividade contínua para parlamentares e servidores, em consonância com a crescente digitalização dos serviços e sistemas disponibilizados pelo Senado Federal."

O contrato terá duração de 48 meses, e a prestação dos serviços está prevista para começar em 1º de fevereiro de 2027. O valor de R$ 6 milhões é uma estimativa. Vencerá a licitação a empresa que apresentar a proposta de menor preço global.

O edital não informa nominalmente quem receberá os aparelhos. Em resposta ao g1, o Senado afirmou que os aparelhos serão destinados aos senadores e alguns diretores. "Os demais modelos atenderão aos cargos de chefia e assessoramento conforme a necessidade da atividade administrativa."

O edital cita o iPhone 17 Pro como modelo de referência, mas prevê o fornecimento da versão mais recente da família Pro da Apple. O documento considera que os novos modelos da empresa são lançados nos meses de setembro e que os aparelhos do contrato serão entregues em janeiro de 2027.

Por isso, afirma que “a tendência é que o aparelho a ser fornecido já seja o iPhone 18 Pro – 512 Gb”, previsto no próprio edital para lançamento em setembro de 2026.

No site oficial da Apple, esse modelo é vendido por valores a partir de R$ 11.999.

De acordo com o Senado, os aparelhos são emprestados pela operadora para uso institucional. "A opção pela contratação dos serviços com fornecimento de aparelhos em comodato, em vez da aquisição direta dos equipamentos, considera critérios de economicidade e eficiência."

Para os outros 330 celulares, o edital cita como referências o Samsung Galaxy A37 5G e o Motorola Moto G86 5G, ou modelos similares.

O documento também estabelece que os iPhones sejam fornecidos nas cores azul, preta ou prateada. Aparelhos com cores exclusivas ou sazonais não serão aceitos. O edital cita como exemplo o laranja-cósmico da geração atual do iPhone Pro.

Além dos 425 celulares, a contratação inclui:

100 modems 4G ou 5G, com franquia mínima de 50 GB;

150 chips para linhas de dados, com franquia mínima de 40 GB;

Reserva estimada de R$ 576 mil para roaming internacional ao longo dos quatro anos de contrato.

A contratação de serviços de telefonia (Pregão 290/2026) tem como finalidade apoiar o exercício dos mandatos parlamentares e as atividades legislativas e administrativas da Casa.

Os aparelhos são emprestados pela operadora para uso institucional. A opção pela contratação dos serviços com fornecimento de aparelhos em comodato, em vez da aquisição direta dos equipamentos, considera critérios de economicidade e eficiência. Nesse modelo, custos decorrentes da obsolescência tecnológica, manutenção e substituição de aparelhos com defeito ficam abrangidos pela contratação.

Soluções semelhantes são adotadas por outros órgãos públicos, como a Procuradoria-Geral da República, o Supremo Tribunal Federal, o Superior Tribunal de Justiça e o Tribunal Superior do Trabalho.

Os aparelhos iPhone 18 Pro previstos no edital serão destinados aos senadores e a alguns diretores. Os demais modelos atenderão aos cargos de chefia e assessoramento conforme a necessidade da atividade administrativa.

A especificação dos equipamentos foi baseada em critérios técnicos, incluindo a compatibilidade com o padrão tecnológico adotado pelo Senado desde 2022, de forma a assegurar continuidade operacional e migração integral de aplicativos e dados.

O valor de aproximadamente R$ 6 milhões corresponde à estimativa da contratação, embasada por pesquisa de preços. O valor final da contratação depende do fim do pregão, uma vez que o critério de julgamento adotado será o de menor preço global.

A futura contratação substituirá o contrato em vigor (CT 170/2022), também disponível para consulta no Portal da Transparência.

articles.title: Chefe da PF rompe com associação em meio a divergências políticas | G1
articles.standfirst: Aliados apontam que Andrei Rodrigues considera que a Associação Nacional dos Delegados de Polícia Federal (ADPF) tem atuado "em defesa de interesses políticos ligados ao bolsonarismo".
articles.summary: Aliados apontam que Andrei Rodrigues considera que a Associação Nacional dos Delegados de Polícia Federal (ADPF) atua "em defesa de interesses políticos ligados ao bolsonarismo".
articles.body:
Andrei Rodrigues, diretor-geral da Polícia Federal — Foto: Divulgação

O diretor-geral da Polícia Federal (PF), Andrei Rodrigues, pediu, na última quinta-feira (5), sua desfiliação da Associação Nacional dos Delegados de Polícia Federal (ADPF) , principal entidade que trata da defesa dos interesses e dos integrantes da categoria.

A decisão ocorre em meio a um desgaste com a ADPF, que, nas palavras de interlocutores do diretor-geral, passou a ser "dominada por um grupo que atua em defesa de interesses políticos ligados ao bolsonarismo".

Integrantes do conselho da entidade estão reunidos na tarde desta terça-feira (10) para definir como vão tratar do assunto — se responder publicamente à decisão de Andrei com uma nota, por exemplo. Contudo, não havia uma definição até a publicação deste post.

Nos bastidores, aliados do diretor-geral apontam uma série de episódios que motivaram o rompimento. Entre eles, apontam aliados de Andrei, a recusa da associação em defender os interesses remuneratórios de 27 superintendentes e diretores da PF, numa discussão sobre a extensão de uma decisão do Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) à corporação.

Outro foco de atrito foi a tentativa da associação de responsabilizar a diretora da Academia Nacional de Polícia pela adoção de uma camiseta padronizada para todos os cargos da instituição. A entidade defendia uma camiseta exclusiva para delegados.

O desgaste também tem um componente político. Na avaliação de aliados de Andrei ouvidos pelo blog , a associação se omitiu diante dos ataques sofridos pela Polícia Federal nos últimos meses, especialmente os promovidos por parlamentares de direita.

Tampouco a ADPF se manifestou, seguem esses interlocutores, na defesa do diretor-geral quando ele foi afastado de suas funções por decisão do ministro do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) André Mendonça, apesar de, à época, ainda integrar o quadro de associados.

Em setembro de 2026, Mendonça determinou o afastamento preventivo de Andrei e do diretor de inteligência da corporação, Leandro Almada, sob a acusação de monitoramento ilegal e "arapongagem institucional" contra o próprio magistrado e contra o advogado-geral da União, Jorge Messias . A ordem acabou revogada pelo ministro Flávio Dino . Posteriormente, Edson Fachin , presidente do STF, suspendeu os atos dos dois colegas de Corte .

A desfiliação expõe um racha entre o comando da Polícia Federal e a entidade representativa dos delegados, em meio a divergências sobre o papel institucional e a atuação política da associação.

articles.title: Lula e Erdogan: Brasil e Turquia discutem parceria em defesa na COP31 | G1
articles.standfirst: Petista teve reunião bilateral com presidente turco em Antália. Os dois também defenderam ampliação do comércio entre os dois países e parcerias estratégicas.
articles.summary: Lula e Erdogan discutem parceria em defesa e ampliação do comércio em Antália, enquanto o Brasil apresenta metas contra o desmatamento e fósseis na COP31.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) se reuniu com o presidente turco, Recep Tayyip Erdogan, às margens da COP 31, realizada na cidade turca de Antália, nesta terça-feira (10).

Segundo o governo brasileiro, os presidentes defenderam a ampliação do comércio entre os dois países e Lula destacou o interesse de estabelecer uma parceria "mais robusta na área de defesa" com a Turquia.

Na reunião, Lula e o líder conservador turco concordaram em trabalhar pela paz e pela defesa do multilateralismo, segundo a nota. O presidente Erdogan se comprometeu a realizar uma visita de Estado ao Brasil em data a ser definida, acompanhado de uma delegação empresarial.

Ainda de acordo com a nota divulgada pelo Palácio do Planalto, o presidente Lula afirmou a Erdogan que a "COP31 representa oportunidade de levar adiante iniciativas lançadas na COP30, em Belém, e colocou-se à disposição para trabalhar pelo êxito da conferência".

Pela previsão do Palácio do Planalto, além de participar da 31ª Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudança do Clima (COP31) na quarta-feira (11), o petista deve ter pelo menos duas reuniões bilaterais:

Quarta-feira (11/11): com o primeiro-ministro do Reino da Noruega, Jonas Gahr Støre;

Quinta-feira (12/11): com o primeiro-ministro do Reino Unido, Andy Burnham.

➡️ COP se refere ao termo em inglês Conferece of Parties, ou Conferência das Partes. A cúpula é um evento anual que reúne representantes de diversos países, além de diplomatas, cientistas, sociedade civil e empresas privadas.

A cúpula de líderes da COP31 acontece nos dias 11 e 12 de novembro, com participação de Lula. O presidente brasileiro transmitirá a presidência da COP à Turquia e à Austrália. A COP30 foi realizada em Belém (PA), no final de 2025.

Na sexta-feira, Lula participou de reunião do Conselho Nacional de Política Energética (CNPE) e destacou que chegaria à COP31 com uma proposta para que o mundo diminua a dependência de combustíveis fósseis.

“O mais importante é que o Brasil não fala teoricamente: o Brasil apresenta propostas. Propostas de um país que descobriu o pré-sal, um país que descobriu muito petróleo na margem equatorial brasileira, e mesmo assim a gente continua sendo país que vai levar avante a diminuição até chegar o dia de não precisar mais de combustível fóssil”, disse.

O presidente também destacou que vai apresentar que a queda das taxas de desmatamento no Brasil e os avanços na implementação do Fundo Florestas Tropicais para Sempre (TFFF).

Interlocutores do governo afirmam que o presidente recebeu pedidos de outros países para encontros, mas, até o momento, nenhuma conversa bilateral foi agendada.

Lula durante reunião com o presidente da Turquia, Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert/PR

João Paulo Capobianco, ministro do Meio Ambiente, afirmou que a presidência brasileira entregará os documentos para reduzir o uso de combustíveis fósseis e para o fim do desmatamento até 2030.

Segundo o ministro do MMA, alguns dos pontos apresentados serão:

Avanços na operação do Fundo Amazônia, “que ficou paralisado nos quatro anos do governo anterior, mas recuperou capacidade de captação de recursos com a ampliação do número de países doadores e já destinou, nos três anos meio do governo Lula, R$ 7,6 bilhões para projetos e programas de proteção e uso sustentável da Amazônia”;

Redução de 560 milhões de toneladas de gases de efeito estufa entre 2022 e 2024;

Redução do desmatamento em todos os biomas brasileiros;

Apresentação do Mapa do Caminho Brasileiro para a Eliminação do Desmatamento e da Degradação Florestal até 2030.

articles.title: WATCH: Jeffries faces uncertainty from incoming Democrats as House speaker vote approaches
articles.summary: New House Democrats say they haven't landed on a House speaker, possibly revealing internal party division over who gets to lead the conference.
articles.body: Several incoming House Democrats are declining to commit to supporting House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., for speaker, exposing potential divisions within the party as it prepares to take control of the lower chamber in January. The uncertainty comes amid criticism from progressive Democratic voters and lawmakers over Jeffries' leadership and political positions, raising questions about whether the New York Democrat will face resistance from members of his own party during the upcoming speaker election. Rep.-elect Adam Hamawy, a progressive New Jersey Democrat who recently appeared on controversial left-wing streamer Hasan Piker's show, told Fox News Digital that he "hasn't decided yet" whether he will support Jeffries. Rep.-elect Patty Garcia, D-Ill., echoed the same uncertainty, saying she would "be united with the progressive caucus" when deciding how to vote. Claire Valdez, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America who was elected to represent New York's 7th Congressional District, declined to comment when asked by Fox News Digital whether she would support Jeffries. Rep.-elect Jamie Ager, D-N.C., also declined to comment, while incoming Texas Democrat Katie Padilla Stout said, "I don't know, we'll see," when asked about her vote. Rep.-elect Fred Wellman, D-Mo., similarly told Fox News Digital that he had not made up his mind, suggesting that other incoming Democrats shared his uncertainty. PROGRESSIVES FUME AT HAKEEM JEFFRIES FOR SAYING DEMOCRATS WON'T 'GET EVEN' WITH TRUMP However, several incoming lawmakers expected to join the Congressional Black Caucus expressed support for Jeffries. "I am for Hakeem Jeffries. There is no doubt about that, he will be a transformative speaker and I truly think that his leadership is going to change the country for the better," Rep.-elect Adrian Boafo told Fox News Digital. "I think our party is on the right track after that historic night," Rep.-elect Jasmine Clark, D-Ga., told Fox News Digital, adding that she would "absolutely" vote for Jeffries. HAKEEM JEFFRIES CONFRONTED ON 'YOU'RE NEXT' CHANTS FOLLOWING NY DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST VICTORIES Rep.-elect Cyril Jefferson, D-N.C., said he was leaning toward supporting Jeffries but wanted the Democratic caucus to have an open discussion about its legislative priorities before selecting its next leader. "We have to make sure that if there are questions and concerns back home, we have to take time and ask those questions, address those concerns and make sure that the priorities we stood on and ran are the concerns the speaker can get Congress to get behind," Jefferson told Fox News Digital. JEFFRIES VOWS DEMOCRATS WON’T ‘GIVE A DIME’ TO TRUMP’S DEPORTATION EFFORTS Rep. Wesley Bell, D-Mo., a member of the Congressional Black Caucus, also expressed his support for Jeffries, telling Fox News Digital that he is "Hakeem Jeffries all the way." Other incoming Democrats, including Scott Wiener, D-Calif., and Brad Lander, D-N.Y., said they support Jeffries for speaker but believe the party should remain open to internal debate over its priorities and direction. "Obviously, people have different approaches of how we'll do that and that's what we are here to figure out," Lander told Fox News Digital. Despite the uncertainty among some incoming members, Lander predicted that Jeffries would be "overwhelmingly elected." articles.title: Hegseth rips impeachment push from outgoing Republican as 'farce,' 'stunt'
articles.summary: War Secretary Pete Hegseth, facing a House impeachment effort, delivers remarks at the first Pengton news conference since May, having focused on the Iran conflict and CENTCOM Strait of Hormuz blockade.
articles.body: War Secretary Pete Hegseth, facing eight articles of impeachment in a privileged House resolution, remains defiant amid kinetic war and political warfare. Hegseth said he stood behind military operations in Iran, Venezuela and Yemen, describing them as lawful. "What one disgruntled and defeated congressman is attempting is not oversight, it's not accountability. It's a political spectacle, a personal manifesto driven by ego and resentment," Hegseth said in a Tuesday morning conference. "Time for one man's final days in Congress to try to do damage to this president, this country and most irresponsibly, the warriors who defend it." "It's a farce, and it's a stunt, and everybody knows it." TRUMP DEFENDS PENTAGON CHIEF AS MASSIE TARGETS HIM: 'HEGSETH SHOULD BE PRAISED, NOT IMPEACHED' President Donald Trump gave a real-time review of Hegseth's remarks in a post Tuesday morning on Truth Social. "Pete Hegseth gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS for his defense against a disgruntled, angry, defeated, former Congressman, Thomas Massie, a TOTAL LOSER!" Trump wrote. "We destroyed terror regimes' capabilities. We sank the boats carrying poison into our communities. We put a narco dictator in handcuffs. These are not high crimes. This is the job, and it's the job well done." "I was proud to execute them, and I would do it again tomorrow," he added. TRUMP GIVES HEGSETH AN ‘A PLUS, PLUS, PLUS’ FOR REJECTION OF WEAPONIZED IMPEACHMENT Hegseth said the impeachment effort hands U.S. enemies a "propaganda victory." "This is not patriotism; this is sabotage. It tells our enemies that the United States will actually punish its own warriors and its own civilian leadership for successfully executing lawful military operations," Hegseth added. Impeachment has been one-sided against Trump, he noted, saying past presidents have been immune amid war efforts. HEGSETH IMPEACHMENT VOTE LOOMS AS HOUSE REPUBLICANS PRIVATELY WARN IT COULD PASS "No secretary of war or secretary of defense has ever been impeached for carrying out lawful military operations and, in our case, successful ones at that," Hegseth said. "Not once – war powers resolution or not." "Not under Reagan in Lebanon, not under Clinton in Kosovo, not under Obama in Iraq and Syria, not under Biden in Iraq and Syria. That's the standard. The history is clear, and it's very straightforward. And one disgruntled congressman wants to shred it over policy disagreements." HEGSETH'S FUTURE DRAWS OMINOUS PREDICTIONS FROM INSIDERS AFTER GOP LOSSES, BUT TRUMP ISN'T BUDGING YET "That's what it is: Policy disagreements," he continued. "Not high crimes, not misdemeanors, not treason, not bribery, not the kinds of offenses the founders intended when they wrote the impeachment clause. "The proper remedy for a policy disagreement: It's legislation; it's debate; it's the next presidential election. It's not handing the House and Senate floor to the Democrats so that they can run a show trial against the president and the secretary of war." REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: HOW MIDTERMS MAY CHANGE THE HOUSE IMPEACHMENT EQUATION FOR HEGSETH Asked about Vance blaming Republican midterm losses on the Iran war, Hegseth said he agreed with the war. "It was done for the right reasons to ensure Iran never gets a nuclear weapon," the war secretary said. Speaking at a G7 summit in France, Secretary of State Marco Rubio weighed in on the impeachment effort. "The president of United States is the commander in chief, and he has a right to defend this country and to address imminent threats that pose a threat to the United States – and he's done so," Rubio told a Paris press gaggle minutes after the Hegseth news conference. "I don't know how anyone could argue that drug dealers trying to import poison into our country is not an imminent threat. It's a real and imminent threat, and it's been addressed." Trump defended Hegseth against Massie's impeachment effort in a Truth Social post Monday night, too, saying his war secretary "should be praised, not impeached." "With recruitment at an ALL-TIME HIGH, from an all-time low under Sleepy Joe Biden, and TWO VICTORIES, Venezuela and Iran, Pete Hegseth should be praised, not Impeached. Congress, stand up for Pete!!!" he added.

articles.title: D.C.'s first Gen Z lawmaker is sworn in. He may be asked to step down soon.
articles.summary: The youngest D.C. lawmaker ever and the first to belong to Generation Z was sworn in to the D.C. Council on Monday before a packed council chamber of support...
articles.body:
The youngest D.C. lawmaker ever and the first to belong to Generation Z was sworn in to the D.C. Council on Monday before a packed council chamber of supporters.

But the milestone may be short-lived. The new at-large council member, 28-year-old Jamal Holtz, the president of D.C. Young Democrats, may only last a few weeks or days in the job, which he accepted after a political chess match over the seat.

After a week of political turmoil, Holtz was appointed by the D.C. Democratic Party to temporarily fill the at-large council seat vacated by Del.-elect Robert C. White Jr. (D). Holtz said he did not ask for the position. And the party made clear it only intended Holtz as a placeholder, announced in a rush last week to block another council member from claiming it.

Holtz said he has not applied for the job and doesn't intend to.

That means a different person could be appointed by the Democratic Party as interim council member as soon as it completes a more formal interview process.

The saga will not end there. There will also be a special election for the seat on April 6, making it possible a new person, again, will claim the seat.

Even Holtz himself acknowledged the circumstances of his appointment were highly unusual, joking that they were reminiscent of "a sixth season of 'House of Cards,'" the Netflix political thriller. But he said he would give to the role the "seriousness, the energy and the commitment" that residents deserved no matter how long he served.

"Because whether you serve for one day or for one decade, the responsibility of public service does not change ," he said.

In a speech before the packed council chamber, Holtz said he would bring his lived experiences as a fourth-generation Washingtonian into the job to advocate for the needs of D.C. residents. He knows what it's like to lose a brother to gun violence, he said. To be homeless and spend days living out of a car, and to watch his mother and others in his life struggle to put food on the table.

"Now I have an opportunity to give back to the city that bought into me ," he said.

The chaotic process surrounding Holtz's appointment kicked off after White's resignation from the D.C. Council last week. Immediately afterward, council member Christina Henderson (I-At Large) attempted to switch her party affiliation to Democrat to slide into the seat, allowing her to rejoin the party ahead of a consequential presidential election and to eventually seek higher office within the city's dominant political party.

But from the vantage point of party faithful, her move was an attempt to "usurp" the party's nomination process as laid out in the D.C. Home Rule Act.

D.C.'s home rule charter caps the number of Democrats who can serve on the council, and Henderson's party switch would have hit the limit. But Henderson stood down on Friday, switching back to independent and clearing the way for Holtz's appointment.

D.C. Council Chairman Phil Mendelson (D) told reporters ahead of the ceremony that he didn't disagree that the process was "confusing and certainly unprecedented." But he said he did not feel he could second-guess the Democratic Party's process and that he had "no choice" but to move ahead with Holtz and, possibly, with a new person if the party goes that route.

At least one former council member, Jack Evans, the former finance committee chairman who spent three decades on the council until his resignation in 2020 amid an ethics probe, said he is applying through the Democratic Party's process and planning to run in the special election.

Chioma Iwuoha, chair of the D.C. Democratic Party, told reporters the party would be meeting again this week to chart its next steps. She did not yet have an exact timeline for a final vote on a potential new appointee.

Asked if Holtz would be considered, she said he had committed to not seeking the role but added: "He has the right to change his mind."

articles.title: GOP lawmaker ousts fellow Republican in gerrymandered California district
articles.summary: Republican Rep. Ken Calvert defeated Rep. Young Kim in a rare GOP vs. GOP battle forced by California Gov. Gavin Newsom's redistricting in the midterms.
articles.body: Gov. Gavin Newsom-signed California redistricting has scored at least a 2-for-1 consolidation of House Republicans. Rep. Ken Calvert, R-Calif., is projected to defeat fellow Rep. Young Kim, R-Calif., in the 40th Congressional District race called Monday night, ostensibly forcing two incumbents to battle for one seat in the gerrymandered district. "I want to congratulate Congressman Ken Calvert on his victory," Kim wrote in a statement posted to X, sharply criticizing the map that effectively drew one of them out. "I wish him the very best as he continues representing our communities. It is unfortunate that Gavin Newsom’s political redistricting scheme forced two Republican members of Congress into this race." AMERICA SAW THE BLUE WAVE COMING — BUT DRASTICALLY UNDERESTIMATED THE EXTENT OF THE DEM TSUNAMI All told, Democrats' redistricting and the so-called blue wave have more than cut the Republican California delegation in half, from nine seats (eight Republicans and one independent that caucuses with them) to just three or four (one race remains too close to call a week after the election). Calvert, the longest-serving Republican in California’s House delegation, had declared victory days earlier while ballots were still being counted. The district covers suburban communities in eastern Orange County and stretches into the Inland Empire in western Riverside County — southeast of Los Angeles. California voters approved the Democratic-backed redistricting plan that combined portions of the two lawmakers' previous districts into a single seat, setting up the rare intraparty contest in one of the state’s remaining Republican strongholds. Kim had represented the area since 2018. Calvert's prior district, which included much of Riverside County and Palm Springs, was carved up and redistributed. ALL THE REPUBLICAN HOUSE MEMBERS OUSTED FROM CONGRESS Calvert is just one of three House Republicans in the state to survive thus far. Rep. Tom McClintock, R-Calif., and Rep. Vince Fong, R-Calif., won re-election in the 5th and 20th Congressional Districts. Those are heavily Republican stretches of the Central Valley and Sierra Nevada foothills — rural agricultural and mountain country well inland, roughly between San Francisco and Los Angeles but far from both coastal metros in the western parts of the state. Rep. Jay Obernolte, R-Calif., is clinging to a narrow lead of just 3,384 votes over Democratic challenger Tessa Lynn Hodge in California's 23rd Congressional District, a High Desert seat in San Bernardino County that was rated Solid R by the Fox News Power Rankings before the midterms. With ballots still being counted, Obernolte holds just a 1.6-point edge — about 50.8% to 49.2% — after winning the district by more than 20 points in 2024. BLUE WAVE NEARLY SWALLOWED SOME OF AMERICA'S REDDEST STATES AS ELECTION DATA EXPOSES GOP'S CLOSE CALLS Four other Republicans from California are leaving Congress in January 2027. Rep. James Gallagher, R-Calif., lost to Democrat Mike McGuire by nearly 13 points, while Rep. David Valadao, R-Calif., lost to Democrat Randy Villegas by nearly 37 points. Rep. Kevin Kiley, I-Calif., who left the Republican Party to try to keep his seat as an independent, lost by more than 17 points to Democrat Richard Pan. Rep. Darrell Issa, R-Calif., did not seek re-election and his former seat flipped to blue under the new map, with Democrat Marni von Wilpert defeating Republican Jim Desmond by nearly 20 points. CALIFORNIA VOTERS DECIDE WHO WILL SUCCEED NEWSOM IN CONSEQUENTIAL GOVERNOR'S RACE He ripped the "gerrymander" effort by Democrats in making California look even deeper blue than it already is. "There are currently no more than four out of what was eight," he told reporters Tuesday morning on Capitol Hill. "If it remains where it is today, then there'll be four or less than 10% of the 52 members. "It's a big change, but it's the result of gerrymandering," he continued. "About 40-45% of the voters in California are Republicans, in presidential races and so on. So you really have called it a 60-40 relationship, and then you have only 10 – less than 10% – so that's what gerrymandering does: It distorts what would otherwise be – not even – but a relatively similar amount of members." Calvert against Kim was the lone GOP vs. GOP battle left by the new map. "As an immigrant who came to the United States in pursuit of the American Dream, serving this nation in Congress has been one of the greatest honors of my life," Kim wrote in her statement posted to X late Monday night. "It has been a privilege to give back to the community that has given me so much, and I am incredibly grateful to my family, our volunteers, supporters, and everyone who placed their trust in me throughout this campaign." DEM WINS TRUMP-TARGETED TEXAS DISTRICT IN REBUKE OF REPUBLICAN REDISTRICTING SHAKEUP Kim said she was proud of the record built "delivering results for our communities, working to secure our country at home and abroad, strengthen our economy, and make life safer and more affordable for California families." During the campaign, both candidates supported President Donald Trump’s agenda early on and later sought to project themselves as pragmatic conservatives. The race turned negative, with Kim citing ethics complaints and an FBI investigation into some of Calvert’s real estate dealings. Calvert denied the allegations and was never charged. Calvert highlighted a campaign donation Kim received from a Chinese American businessman who has faced scrutiny over alleged foreign influence. Kim returned the contribution and said she was unaware of the claims. "With the passage of Prop 50, Californians were sold a bill of goods, allowing Gavin Newsom and his radical allies in Sacramento an unprecedented power grab to redraw the Congressional map and silence those who disagree with his extreme policies," Calvert wrote on X a year ago. "Gerrymandering districts because you don’t like the results of an election is politics at its absolute worst. articles.title: Explosive House report exposes failures it says allowed Epstein's abuse to continue for years
articles.summary: House Republicans uncovered alleged conflicts of interest involving federal prosecutors and failures by financial institutions that enabled Epstein's yearslong abuse.
articles.body: FIRST ON FOX: The House Oversight Committee released a report concluding that prosecutorial failures, preferential treatment and institutional negligence allowed Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell to continue sexually exploiting young women and girls for years. The investigation, led by Chairman James Comer, R-Ky., raised concerns about potential conflicts of interest involving federal prosecutors, financial institutions that overlooked warning signs of sex trafficking and individuals accused of facilitating Epstein's abuse. The report identified two former federal prosecutors whose involvement in Epstein's original investigation raised potential conflicts of interest. Matthew Menchel, a senior federal prosecutor who recommended resolving Epstein's case through a non-prosecution agreement, previously had a romantic relationship with Lilly Ann Sanchez, who later represented Epstein. Menchel did not recuse himself from the investigation and continued communicating and meeting with Epstein after the agreement, according to documents cited by the committee. TODD BLANCHE SAYS 'NO CLOSED INVESTIGATIONS' IN EPSTEIN CASE, VOWS DOJ WILL PURSUE NEW SUSPECTS Investigators also learned of an alleged photograph showing Menchel skiing with Epstein in Colorado in the early 2000s but could not verify its existence or establish that Menchel's decisions were improperly influenced. Menchel, however, denied ever having skied with Epstein in a statement to the Miami Herald but did not deny meeting with him after leaving the U.S. Attorney's Office. His attorneys said their correspondence concerned potential legal representation and referrals, none of which resulted in business. His attorneys also maintained that Menchel was not responsible for the final plea agreement, which was more lenient than the arrangement he recommended. A 2020 Justice Department Office of Professional Responsibility report found that Menchel failed to disclose his relationship with Sanchez to supervisors but found no evidence of prosecutorial misconduct. Sanchez did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. Former federal prosecutor Bruce Reinhart established a private law practice while employed by the U.S. Attorney's Office and later represented Epstein associates. His practice was involved in matters related to Epstein's work-release program. Former U.S. Attorney Alexander Acosta testified that he did not know whether Reinhart had access to information about the Epstein investigation. Reinhart did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. The committee said it urged the Justice Department to investigate further former Miami Beach Mayor Philip Levine and celebrity hairstylist Frédéric Fekkai further, following testimony from Sarah Kellen, a former Epstein assistant who alleged that Epstein and the two associates sexually abused her. Both Levine and Fekkai have denied the allegations in earlier statements. Levine and Fekkai did not respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment. Kellen also testified that Epstein instructed another assistant to remove computers, hard drives and other equipment from his Palm Beach residence before authorities searched the property in 2005. Investigators believed the equipment could contain evidence of sexual exploitation. Epstein's attorney, Darren Indyke, testified that he later learned the hard drives were in the possession of private investigators. Federal investigators identified a potential lead concerning the equipment but abandoned the effort before finalizing Epstein's non-prosecution agreement. The report also examined whether Sandy Berger, former national security advisor to President Bill Clinton, warned Epstein about the search, given that he sent Epstein an urgent message 18 days before the search. However, the committee found no evidence establishing that Berger tipped him off or that the message concerned the investigation. CLINTON JUDGE ORDERS DOJ TO UNSEAL THE EPSTEIN FILES IT HAS BEEN KEEPING HIDDEN The committee recommended further investigations, stronger protections for trafficking survivors and reforms to prevent similar federal law enforcement failures. Among those recommended for further investigation was Lesley Groff, Epstein's executive assistant for nearly two decades. Groff, who scheduled Epstein's daily massage appointments and coordinated travel and lodging for women visiting his properties, testified that she was unaware he was sexually abusing young women and girls. Groff continued working for Epstein after his 2008 conviction. Groff did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. The committee also criticized Epstein's treatment following his 2008 conviction, arguing that his work-release privileges allowed him to continue abusing women. Epstein served approximately 13 months of an 18-month sentence and was permitted to leave jail for up to 12 hours daily, six days a week. His privileges included working at the Florida Science Foundation, which the committee described as a sham organization, traveling in private vehicles accompanied by paid off-duty sheriff's deputies, meeting visitors without continuous monitoring and visiting his Palm Beach residence. Kellen and other survivors alleged that Epstein continued sexually abusing them during his work release. The investigation also examined Epstein's relationships with prominent politicians, business executives and academic institutions, including billionaire Bill Gates and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. Lutnick told the Oversight Committee in 2026 that he had "done absolutely nothing wrong." He acknowledged visiting Epstein's private island for lunch with his family in 2012, despite previously claiming he had cut ties with Epstein in 2005. Lutnick said he could not recall why his family had lunch there. Comer said Lutnick addressed the discrepancy in his opening statement. Gates testified that Epstein requested reimbursement for expenses involving a woman with whom Gates had an affair. Gates said he refused to pay, ended his relationship with Epstein in late 2014 and was never a client of Epstein's financial businesses. Gates and Lutnick did not respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment. The committee also identified billionaire financier Leon Black as a major source of Epstein's income following his 2008 conviction. Black paid Epstein approximately $158 million to $170 million for purported tax and estate planning services. The committee identified an agreement involving a woman with whom Black had an extramarital relationship that reportedly required payments of $100,000 per month for 15 years, among other benefits, in exchange for confidentiality. Epstein reportedly advised Black on the agreement. Black cited an independent investigation that found he was not involved in Epstein's criminal activities, although the committee questioned its independence. EPSTEIN-LINKED BILLIONAIRE POURS $500K INTO SUPER PAC BACKING KENTUCKY DEMOCRAT: 'DIRTY EPSTEIN-CLASS MONEY' Black also refused to fully answer certain committee questions and failed to comply with subpoenas, prompting a unanimous House vote in September 2026 to hold him in criminal contempt of Congress. Black did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. The report also examined Epstein's relationships with current and former public officials. Kathryn Ruemmler, former White House counsel under President Barack Obama, maintained a professional relationship with Epstein after his 2008 conviction and received expensive gifts, including designer handbags, boots, spa services and travel upgrades. In a 2016 email, Ruemmler joked about receiving the "best massage ever but not your kind of massage." Ruemmler acknowledged that the remark was in poor taste and testified that she believed Epstein had resolved his criminal case and was living lawfully. She also testified that a May 2019 meeting with Epstein concerned potential litigation threatened by attorney Michael Avenatti, not a criminal investigation. The report identified Del. Stacey Plaskett, D-V.I., as having exchanged text messages with Epstein during a 2019 congressional hearing, including communications about questioning a witness. Plaskett did not deny exchanging the messages. Her office said she received texts from staff, constituents and members of the public, including Epstein, whom she described as a constituent who contacted her following a widely circulated hearing exchange. The committee did not allege wrongdoing by Plaskett. Ruemmler and Plaskett did not respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment. The report also cited an email indicating that House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries' campaign solicited a donation from Epstein. Jeffries, however, said he had no recollection of the email and had never met or communicated with Epstein. Federal election records reportedly show no donations from Epstein to Jeffries or the committees involved. Reports identified Lisa Rossi of the political consulting firm Dynamic SRG as the sender of the message. Jeffries did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. EXCLUSIVE: OSSOFF CHALLENGED TO RETURN EPSTEIN-LINKED DONATION OR RETRACT ‘EPSTEIN CLASS’ ATTACK CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Regarding Epstein's death in 2019, the committee identified serious prison security failures but did not overturn the official suicide finding. The report also criticized the Justice Department for missing disclosure deadlines and exposing survivors' personal information during the release of millions of Epstein-related documents. The Republican-led investigation stated that it uncovered no evidence implicating President Donald Trump in Epstein's criminal activities and accused congressional Democrats of politicizing the investigation.

articles.title: Hegseth impeachment: What is he accused of, and could he be removed?
articles.summary: Eight articles brought by a Republican lawmaker accuse US Pentagon chief of waging unlawful wars on Iran and Venezuela.
articles.body:
US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth is facing possible impeachment after Republican Congressman Thomas Massie introduced a resolution to remove him from office.

On Monday, Massie took the floor of the House of Representatives to accuse Hegseth of carrying out unlawful orders and contravening the United States Constitution by waging war against Iran and Venezuela, as well as systematically failing to protect civilians.

He introduced eight articles of impeachment on Monday, starting a two-day countdown that could bring a vote by midweek.

Top Democrats say they will support the resolution, while Hegseth has struck a defiant tone and has the backing of US President Donald Trump.

The US Constitution gives the House of Representatives “the sole Power of Impeachment”, meaning it alone can choose to initiate impeachment proceedings against senior officials, including cabinet members.

Officials can be impeached and removed for “Treason, Bribery, or other high Crimes and Misdemeanors”.

If a majority of the House votes to impeach a cabinet member, the Senate then gets to decide by majority whether to acquit or to convict and remove them. Conviction requires a two-thirds majority of Senate votes.

President Trump made history during his first term in office by becoming the only US president to be impeached by a Democrat-held House twice, though he was acquitted by a Republican-held Senate twice.

If impeached, Hegseth would be the second head of the US military to meet that fate since William Belknap, who was impeached for bribery in 1876.

In this case, Hegseth stands accused of “high crimes and misdemeanors” over his handling of the war on Iran and the conflict with Venezuela.

Of the eight articles, four concern Iran and two cover Venezuela and strikes on boats conducted in the Caribbean since 2025. One relates to the 2025 US air campaign in Yemen. The only non-conflict-related article is Hegseth’s treatment of Democratic Senator Mark Kelly.

Kelly, an Arizona Democrat and retired US Navy captain, appeared with five other Democratic lawmakers in a November 2025 video telling US troops: “Our laws are clear. You can refuse illegal orders.”

Hegseth accused them of sedition and threatened to prosecute them, while Trump said in a social media post that their conduct was “punishable by DEATH!”

Massie’s articles accuse Hegseth of trying to subject the speech and oversight activities of members of Congress “to the will and discretion” of the Department of Defense.

What do the articles say about Iran, Venezuela and Yemen?

Massie said that while Trump was culpable for issuing what he described as unlawful orders, like attacking Iran, Hegseth chose to carry them out.

“Hegseth should not carry out illegal orders, and that’s why we’re impeaching him,” Massie said.

Three of the four Iran articles rest on the War Powers Resolution, a 1973 law that limits a president’s power to wage war without the approval of Congress.

Going to war without the approval of Congress or an attack on the US.

Ignoring a resolution passed by both chambers of Congress in June that ordered US forces out of the fighting.

Continuing the war after a 60-day limit for unauthorised hostilities ran out on May 1.

Taking measures to “systematically dismantle civilian-protection infrastructure”, and responsibility for the Minab school strike that killed 156 civilians, mostly children, on the first day of the war.

The articles accuse Hegseth of fostering a culture “hostile to the law of armed conflict and the protection of civilians”. They cite his declaration in September 2025, as he rebranded the Department of Defense as the Department of War: “Maximum lethality, not tepid legality. Violent effect, not politically correct.”

At a media briefing on Monday, Massie dismissed a claim that the Minab school strike was a mistake caused by the fog of war, saying the US had months to prepare its unilateral attack on Iran.

“There’s no fog of war on the first day,” he said.

In January, US special forces abducted former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, in a raid on Caracas , after months of US strikes on alleged drug boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific.

Committing an act of war against Venezuela without the approval of Congress by abducting Maduro.

Using drug enforcement as cover for a bid to control Venezuela’s oil.

Carrying out the extrajudicial killings of at least 243 people in at least 69 boat strikes since September 2025, mostly in international waters.

Denying quarter to shipwrecked targets who posed no threat and striking them again .

Massie dismissed the administration’s description of the raid on Maduro as a law enforcement operation.

“It was to kidnap a foreign leader so we could take their oil,” he said.

Regarding the US bombing campaign against Yemen’s Houthi group in 2025, Hegseth is accused of:

Launching the campaign without a declaration of war, approval from Congress, or an attack on the US, in breach of the War Powers Resolution.

Pressing ahead even though Trump did not notify Congress until 13 days after the strikes began.

Directing an operation that killed an estimated 224 civilians.

Ordering the strikes knowing there was no imminent threat.

The article cites a leaked Signal chat between Hegseth and other senior Trump administration officials involved in the planning and execution of the Yemen attack.

Massie said everyone in the chat agreed there was no imminent threat that would justify bypassing Congress. “The consequence of that was civilians killed,” he said.

Hegseth held a press conference on Tuesday where he struck a defiant tone.

“It’s a farce, and it’s a stunt,” he said, referring to the impeachment motion. “And everybody knows it.”

Arguing that the conflicts he oversaw were “lawful military operations”, he castigated Massie for trying to impeach him for what he called “policy disagreements”.

“The proper remedy for a policy disagreement is legislation,” he said. “It’s debate. It’s the next presidential election. It’s not handing the House and Senate floor to Democrats so they can run a show trial against the president and Secretary of War.”

He defended his track record and the US campaigns in Iran and Latin America while warning that punishing him would be the first step in prosecuting soldiers for “doing their job”.

“If they want to come after the warriors, they’re going to have to come through me,” he said.

He compared his situation to Trump’s two impeachments and acquittals during his first term, saying that the president had “come back stronger”.

Trump, for his part, has said that he would stand by Hegseth even if he is impeached, calling Massie a “stone-cold loser”.

Republicans control the House until January 3, when Democrats take over. If most Democrats follow their House leader, Hakeem Jeffries , who says he is a “hard yes”, Massie would only need a handful of Republicans to support the resolution.

Conviction is another story. Even if the House chooses to impeach, Republicans currently hold 53 of the Senate’s 100 seats, and Democrats, expected to have about 54 next year, would still fall far short of the 67 supermajority of votes needed to oust Hegseth from office.

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer, expected to become Senate majority leader once the new Congress is seated, has said that Hegseth “must stand trial before the Senate”.

Massie, meanwhile, has urged Trump to act first.

“President Trump should replace Secretary Hegseth now while he can still get a replacement confirmed in the Senate,” he said.
